title: Abba Yosi ben Chanan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Mishnah, Middot ch. 2, mishnah 6, which says that the thirteen prostrations correspond to the thirteen gates. And in Pesachim 57a: Abba Shaul ben Batnit said in the name of Abba Yosef ben Hanin (Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim cites a variant reading, Abba Yosi ben Hanan): Woe is me because of the house of Boethus — because of the house of Katros — because of the house of Yishmael ben Piakhu, etc.
Hyman concludes: “From this we see that he lived in the time of the Second Temple.”

And in Zevachim65a he says: He takes it and takes its gizzard together with it (regarding the pinching of a bird offering); and in Sotah20b: if she has merit, it suspends [the punishment] for her for three months — the words of Abba Yosi ben Hanan; R-A ben Yitzchak, a man of Kfar Darom, says — R' Yishmael says.

Hyman suggests: Possibly [this wording] belongs to the editors of the Gemara, who said, “Whose view is the Mishnah? Not Abba Yosi,” etc.; it does not mean that he disputed with them, since he was much earlier than they were.

Hyman gives the following readings: In Temurah12b: Yosef ben Honi says: In two and three vessels, it invalidates the mikveh. And in the Tosefta, Mikvaot ch. 3, the reading is Abba Shaul ben Honi; the G-R-A reading is Abba Yosi ben Honi; and in the Zuckermandel Tosefta the reading is Abba Yosi ben Hanan. And there is

notes.text: Sotah20b spells out Rabbi Elazar ben Yitzchak and explicitly asks whose view the Mishnah represents, excluding the named positions. Hyman’s suggestion about editorial arrangement concerns that formulation, not Abba Yosi being a late editor. Korqevan is the gizzard. The notice ends with a transition “And there is,” whose continuation is not supplied.
